management_steps.details: ABCD. Keep NPO. Insert 2x large-bore IVs. Administer warm Balsol/Ringer's Lactate (10ml/kg).

Transfuse PRCs if haemodynamically unstable despite crystalloid bolus, Hb < 7 in low-risk, or Hb < 9 in high-risk/elderly/coronary disease. If coagulopathic (INR > 1.5) or on Warfarin: give FFP 10-20ml/kg or PCC.

Give Pantoprazole (Pantoloc) 80mg IV loading dose, then start infusion (200mg in 200ml N/S at 8 ml/hr). If variceal/cirrhosis: give Ceftriaxone 1g IV + Octreotide 50mcg bolus followed by 50mcg/hr infusion.
Notify surgical/gastroenterology registrar on call urgently. Consider Sengstaken-Blakemore tube if catastrophic variceal bleeding.

warnings: Avoid over-transfusion in suspected variceal bleeds (increases portal pressure and worsens haemorrhage).
There is NO role for Tranexamic Acid (TXA) in upper GI bleeding.
